definition_one_sentence: a customer with at least one order not cancelled in the last 12 months (this is the number given to the board)
formula_or_rule: count distinct customer_id where status is not cancelled and order_date is in the last 12 months
example: on 2026-11-25 a customer with a delivered order on 2026-03-10 is active - if his only order was cancelled he is not. Today we have 1080 active customers (1104 if we wrongly count cancelled orders)
related_columns: fct_orders.status / fct_orders.order_date (dim_customers.last_order_date is not enough because it includes cancelled orders)
notes_conflicts: Sales wanted 6 months and Finance 12 months. The CDO decided: 12 months is the official definition because investors compare years. Sales keeps its 6 months view but with another name (recently active customer)

definition_one_sentence: a customer with at least one order not cancelled in the last 6 months (used by Sales for campaigns - not for the board)
formula_or_rule: same rule as active customer but with 6 months
example: on 2026-11-25 a customer with an order on 2026-07-01 is recently active. With an order on 2026-03-10 he is active but not recently active. Today we have 775
notes_conflicts: new term created to solve the conflict on active customer (one term = one definition). A recently active customer is always an active customer too

definition_one_sentence: what ShopFast really earns on an order: what the customer paid minus refunds and without VAT (shipping included)
example: customer pays 120 € and no refund = 100 €. Customer pays 120 € and gets 24 € back = (120 - 24) / 1.20 = 80 €
notes_conflicts: Sales used net revenue with VAT. Decision: the VAT is not ShopFast money so net revenue is always without VAT. Sales commissions are based on gross revenue (with VAT) which is another term

definition_one_sentence: a customer who already ordered but has no order (not cancelled) in the last 12 months
formula_or_rule: at least 1 order not cancelled in the past and not an active customer
example: a customer whose last order was on 2025-06-15 is churned on 2026-11-25. A customer who never ordered is not churned
notes_conflicts: it is the opposite of active customer (also 12 months) so active + churned + never ordered = all customers. It is what the churn model tries to predict

definition_one_sentence: a customer account on ShopFast (one customer_id) even if it never ordered
formula_or_rule: one row in dim_customers = one customer
example: 1233 accounts after removing the exact duplicates (1241 rows in raw). 52 people have 2 accounts with the same email and for now they count as 2 customers
notes_conflicts: customer = account and not person. To count persons we would need to merge the duplicate accounts (is_duplicate_email from CTP 2) and the Steward has to decide that

definition_one_sentence: an order made by a customer on any channel whatever its status (pending / shipped / delivered / cancelled / returned)
formula_or_rule: one row in fct_orders = one order
example: 5200 orders in fct_orders after removing 7 duplicate order_id. A cancelled order is still an order but it does not count in KPIs that remove cancelled orders
notes_conflicts: cancelled orders stay in the table so each KPI has to say if it removes them or not (active customer removes them)
